gui.distantstock.manual.p1: First tune a Distant Terminal to a local Create logistics network. You can create a Distant Stock network and obtain its long-lived join code. On another server, tune a terminal to that server’s local Create network and join it with the same code. The terminal can then switch between warehouse members of that Distant Stock network.
gui.distantstock.manual.p2: The warehouse can use the pale-blue Distant Packager. It keeps Create packing logic and produces Distant Parcels. Face the dock cabin toward the operator and leave the sides free for a belt or hopper. An import dock matches address only (blank = *). A parcel in the bay means the slots are occupied.
gui.distantstock.manual.p3: Players never type an IP. OP runs /distantstock, or sneak-clicks a monitor. Pick Host (warehouse) or Client (outer), fill self id, listen, peer, password. Save writes this server's config/distantstock-common.toml and restarts the listener. Same password on every side.
gui.distantstock.manual.p4: One warehouse, many survival servers. Orders carry from=self.id. After packing, the warehouse POSTs the package only to that origin. Outer servers pull /stock from the host only. Outer servers do not act as warehouses for each other.
gui.distantstock.manual.p5: Goggles show live data only: dock mode, short freq or address, UP/DOWN, slots or backlog. Desk: freq, address, catalog size. Monitor: TPS and queue. The tutorial lives in this book. Set giveManual=false to stop handing one out on first join.

block.distantstock.dock.desc: Full casing, pipes into the sides and a fallback face underneath that needs a chute. Lamp: off = offline, green = standby, cyan blinking = dispatching, orange blinking = fallback blocked, red = fault.
block.distantstock.tower_casing.desc: Decorative casing with connected textures on all six faces. A redstone signal turns the centre of linked casings into a see-through window; the propagation range is configurable.
block.distantstock.tower_core.desc: The centre of the tower’s 3x3 base, driven by rotation from below. Stack couplers on top of it and cap them with an ether resonator to raise a tower.
block.distantstock.tower_coupler.desc: A segment of the mast. The taller the stack, the higher the tier — and the more distant devices and chunks it carries.
block.distantstock.ether_resonator.desc: The cap. Turning arms mean the tower is running; it only starts once the tower is complete.
block.distantstock.gauge.desc: A stock desk for the floor. Write to it with a terminal that has joined a network.
block.distantstock.monitor.desc: Wall dashboard: local/peer TPS and link pressure. OP sneak-click opens link setup.
block.distantstock.remote_packager.desc: A pale-blue Create packager variant. It keeps addresses and contents while producing Distant Parcels.

distantstock.ponder.distant_export.text_: Orders are packed at the warehouse, exactly like Create logistics.
Move the sealed parcel to a Distant Dock with normal Create logistics.
The dock takes one parcel and sends it through the Distant Stock link.
Keep the underside clear: returned or rejected parcels leave from here.

gui.distantstock.manual.p7: A receiving address decides which distant docks can receive a parcel. Address names are unique inside one Distant Stock network and may be public or unlisted. Unlisted only hides them from ordinary lists; anyone who knows the exact address may still deliver to it. Use a terminal to attach docks to an address and select that address for orders.
gui.distantstock.manual.p8: A Distant Gauge replenishes toward its stock target, while a Distant Redstone Requester submits its preset order on a rising redstone edge. Use a tuned terminal to bind them to a warehouse member and receiving address in the same Distant Stock network. Both require tower coverage.
distantstock.ponder.distant_replenish.te: A Distant Gauge watches one item and maintains the amount you set.
Bind each gauge slot to a tuned Requester to choose its remote warehouse.
The Distant Redstone Requester sends its configured order on a rising edge.
Both order into the receiving group; the goods arrive through its dock.

gui.distantstock.manual.p9: For cross-server transport, both ends must be covered by running towers. Attach receiving docks to the target receiving address, then select that address at the sending side. Parcels are packed at the source warehouse, cross through distant docks, and enter local Create logistics using the local package address after arrival. The underside remains the return face.

Diagnostic Frogport bound to Create network %s
Bind the Diagnostic Frogport to a tuned Create logistics node first
Normal Frogports keep their normal addresses; Distant Stock does not replace Create routing.
A Diagnostic Frogport probes the route and catches parcels that truly have no destination.
When a real destination stalls, the Cache Frogport temporarily takes its address.
Its 54-slot buffer is a real inventory: take any parcel out manually if needed.
When the route recovers, untouched parcels are replayed automatically.
distantstock.ponder.distant_logger.text_: The Logger records active warnings and faults for the network it watches.
Acknowledge to silence the alarm; acknowledgement does not erase the fault.
AC remains until the incident slip is printed; without paper you may only silence it.
Stack lights and sounders turn those same conditions into a room-scale Andon.
